page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4n family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This compute-centric allocation ratio is designed for workloads requiring higher processing power relative to memory capacity.

This server configuration does not include bundled local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached block storage options. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance. The lack of integrated local storage and hardware accelerators, such as GPUs, represents a tradeoff, positioning this instance strictly for non-graphical, compute-focused tasks that rely on network-attached storage.

The qualitative cost profile of the c4n-highcpu-8 is aligned with compute-optimized workloads where paying for excess memory is inefficient. Appropriate workloads for this instance include compute-bound applications, batch processing, web serving, and lightweight containerized microservices that do not require local SSD performance or GPU acceleration.
